subject: physics
question_text: Why does a heavy rifle not recoil as strongly as a light rifle using the same cartridges?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 5 VERY SHORT ANSWER. The 1+1 mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Momentum is conserved
lines: M, V → rifle;   m, v → bullet
steps.margin_note: Define the four symbols in one line. An unlabelled M costs the mark.
steps.why: The cartridge fixes the bullet side of this equation. Whatever m v it produces, the rifle must match it.
common_mistakes: Writing M V = m v without saying which letters are the rifle.

recall.must_convey: That the momentum of the rifle equals the momentum of the bullet, by conservation of momentum.

steps.label: Why heavier means less
lines: The same cartridge gives the same m v,
so a heavier rifle recoils more slowly.
steps.margin_note: The mark is for the inverse relation — write V ∝ 1/M, not just "it is heavy".
steps.why: Recoil VELOCITY is what bruises a shoulder, and it is the momentum divided by the mass. Same momentum, more mass, less speed.
common_mistakes: Answering "because it is heavy" with no relation written.

recall.must_convey: That the recoil velocity is inversely proportional to the mass of the rifle.
accept: recoil velocity is inversely proportional to mass
V is inversely proportional to M
